key_findings.value: At 525 °C the α matrix of the 19Al alloy stays almost featureless even after 10 h of aging, consistent with the very slow β-Mn precipitation.

unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy, aging at 525 °C is the mildest aging condition studied: hardness rises only slightly from 562.3 ± 8.9 HV (1 h) to 614.4 ± 17.3 HV (10 h), and the α→β-Mn transformation is far from complete (only 12.1 % β-Mn after 10 h).

The increase in Al content slows the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn during low-temperature aging; at 525 °C only a small amount of β-Mn formed in the 19Al alloy even after 10 h, whereas the 15Al alloy almost completely transformed to β-Mn within 3 h at 525 °C.
The β-Mn primarily precipitated along α grain boundaries, while a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn was also observed within the α grains for the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C.
